rights: You have the right to a written rental agreement with clear terms — oral agreements are harder to enforce.
Security deposit cannot exceed the limit set by your state's Rent Control Act (typically 1-3 months' rent).
The landlord must provide reasonable notice before seeking eviction — eviction can only be on grounds specified in the applicable Rent Control Act.
Essential services (water, electricity) cannot be cut off by the landlord to force eviction.
Structural repairs are generally the landlord's responsibility; only routine maintenance may be the tenant's.
Rent cannot be increased beyond the limit set by the Rent Control Act (where applicable) without proper notice.
You have the right to receive a receipt for every rent payment made.
The landlord cannot enter the premises without reasonable notice except in emergency.
Upon vacating, you are entitled to the return of your security deposit minus legitimate deductions for damage beyond normal wear and tear.
